structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, then in hollow-horned ruminants (Bovidae) the left and right horns of individual animals have the same shape parameters (length, basal circumference, spiral curvature and torsion) with opposite handedness, so left-minus-right differences in size and shape are centred on zero and small relative to between-individual variation.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In a per-individual bovid dataset with separate left and right horn measurements or 3D horn landmarks (n >= 30 individuals), the median absolute asymmetry |R-L|/((R+L)/2) of horn length is <= 5%, the mean signed asymmetry is not significantly different from 0 (|mean| < 2%, paired t-test p > 0.05), and the intra-class correlation between L and mirrored R is >= 0.95. For helical horns, the left and right spiral handedness must be opposite in >= 95% of individuals.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The median absolute horn-length asymmetry exceeds 10%, or the mean signed asymmetry differs significantly from 0 with |mean| >= 2%, or the L/mirrored-R intra-class correlation is below 0.90, or the two horns have the same handedness in more than 5% of helical-horned individuals.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's "conjugate spirals" and "mirror-image" map onto two measurable quantities. The first is the paired left/right difference in horn length, circumference and spiral parameters. The second is the opposite chirality of the two horns, tested by reflecting one horn's landmarks and comparing shape. Real horns carry fluctuating asymmetry, so the test uses approximate mirror symmetry within a tolerance rather than exact symmetry. No public per-individual bovid horn dataset was found and fetched, so no dataset is named.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: Searches of Dryad (including its API), plus general web searches, turned up no public per-individual dataset of bovid horn measurements with separate left and right values. The Dryad hits were beetle horns, calf disbudding wound healing, and mule deer antlers, which are cervid antlers rather than hollow horns. The relevant bovid studies (Sanmartinero creole cattle, Catalan goats, Alpine ibex) have no data deposit that I could confirm. I did not name any identifier I could not fetch and verify.

input.hypothesis: If the claim holds, then in hollow-horned ruminants (Bovidae) the left and right horns of individual animals have the same shape parameters (length, basal circumference, spiral curvature and torsion) with opposite handedness, so left-minus-right differences in size and shape are centred on zero and small relative to between-individual variation.
input.pass_criterion: In a per-individual bovid dataset with separate left and right horn measurements or 3D horn landmarks (n >= 30 individuals), the median absolute asymmetry |R-L|/((R+L)/2) of horn length is <= 5%, the mean signed asymmetry is not significantly different from 0 (|mean| < 2%, paired t-test p > 0.05), and the intra-class correlation between L and mirrored R is >= 0.95. For helical horns, the left and right spiral handedness must be opposite in >= 95% of individuals.
input.fail_criterion: The median absolute horn-length asymmetry exceeds 10%, or the mean signed asymmetry differs significantly from 0 with |mean| >= 2%, or the L/mirrored-R intra-class correlation is below 0.90, or the two horns have the same handedness in more than 5% of helical-horned individuals.
input.interpretation: Thompson's "conjugate spirals" and "mirror-image" map onto two measurable quantities. The first is the paired left/right difference in horn length, circumference and spiral parameters. The second is the opposite chirality of the two horns, tested by reflecting one horn's landmarks and comparing shape. Real horns carry fluctuating asymmetry, so the test uses approximate mirror symmetry within a tolerance rather than exact symmetry. No public per-individual bovid horn dataset was found and fetched, so no dataset is named.
